question: alt+enter in a Claude pane sometimes opens a line and sometimes sends the message. Where does the alt go?

browserHalf.how: probe.py — Chrome 152.0.7977.64 headless, CDP Input.dispatchKeyEvent (the browser's own input pipeline, not a synthesised DOM event) against handler.js, which is the installDom block copied verbatim out of PaneTextInput.wasmJs.kt
browserHalf.chordWhileTheCanvasHoldsTheFocus: keydown lands on the canvas, the handler never sees it, nothing is queued at all
browserHalf.verdict: The browser is not the bug. Chrome carries altKey on the first keydown after a focus change exactly as on the tenth, and a focus strand produces silence rather than a bare Enter, so it cannot be what drops the alt.

ptyHalf.how: ptysplit.py — a child blocked in read(0) on a raw pty, its read boundaries logged; ESC and CR written one way or another, 5 trials each
ptyHalf.twoWritesNoGap: b'\x1b\r' — one read, 5/5 (the writer beats the reader to the scheduler)
ptyHalf.verdict: ESC and CR are alt+enter only while they arrive in one read. The threshold is somewhere under 1 ms, and a node-to-herdr pane.send_text round trip is 1-3 ms (#273).

cause: InputSink.raw cut every payload carrying \r or \n in two whenever a SubmitGuard was attached — which is every pane on screen — and emitted each half as its own `input` message, whether or not the guard actually held anything back.
